acquisitions.title: What to know about the landmark Warner Bros. Discovery sale
acquisitions.excerpt: Warner Bros. Discovery explored a potential sale of its assets after struggling with heavy debt, declining cable viewership, and streaming competition. Netflix initially reached an agreement in December to acquire Warner's studios and streaming platforms for $82.7 billion. However, a bidding war developed when Paramount pursued a broader acquisition of all Warner assets. Although the Warner board initially rejected Paramount's advances due to debt concerns and foreign sovereign wealth fund backing, Paramount increased its offer to $31 per share in February. Netflix subsequently declined to match the higher bid and withdrew from negotiations. Paramount's successful $111 billion bid covered film and television studios, HBO, streaming services, games, and networks such as CNN and HGTV. The transaction faced significant regulatory hurdles and political scrutiny, including a lawsuit filed in July by a coalition of twelve state attorneys general to block the merger. Following approvals by the Department of Justice and a federal judge, the acquisition became official on October 6. The newly combined corporation was renamed Skydance, with plans to eventually integrate Paramount+, HBO Max, and Discovery+.

acquisitions.title: AWS Weekly Roundup: Welcome DuckLabs to the team, Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD), and more (August 31, 2026)
acquisitions.excerpt: Amazon Web Services has signed a definitive agreement to acquire DuckLabs, an Amsterdam-based company behind the popular open-source analytical database DuckDB. DuckDB runs in-process and executes SQL directly against files such as Parquet, CSV, and JSON. Following the acquisition, DuckDB will remain open source under an independent foundation and the MIT license. Co-founders Hannes Mühleisen and Mark Raasveldt will continue leading the technical direction of the project. DuckDB can operate locally or on Amazon S3, delivering high performance for everyday queries under a terabyte in size. AWS plans to integrate DuckDB's query speed with enterprise-scale services including Amazon S3, Amazon Redshift, and Amazon Athena. The database also pairs effectively with AI agents as they experiment and navigate through data sets. Additionally, AWS intends to combine the technology with further analytics and machine learning offerings such as Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, and Amazon SageMaker. Further details regarding the transaction and the evolving landscape of analytics were discussed by Vice President and Distinguished Engineer Andy Warfield in a post on the All Things Distributed blog.

launches.title: Smart ring maker Ultrahuman to roll out biological-age model across UAE
launches.excerpt: Health tech startup Ultrahuman has partnered with the Abu Dhabi Public Health Center to develop and validate a biological-age model for residents across the United Arab Emirates. The two-year memorandum of understanding involves combining clinical biomarkers with data from wearable devices to estimate individual ageing rates and identify influencing factors such as sleep, metabolism, and cardiovascular health. The initiative marks the Bengaluru-based company's first deployment of its health algorithms at a national scale, moving beyond its core business of selling smart rings. The biological-age model is designed to be wearable-agnostic, meaning it can ingest data from various devices including wrist-worn gadgets, patches, and straps alongside clinical markers. Individuals will eventually be able to access their health age through government digital health platforms such as Sahatna and TAMM. Ultrahuman CEO Mohit Kumar noted that the UAE is already among the company's ten largest markets, accounting for roughly four to five percent of overall revenue. The underlying model was built using Ultrahuman's existing data to track how health markers change with chronological age, although the algorithmic model will be deployed locally without the startup accessing personally identifiable information. The partnership comes as smart ring competitors Ultrahuman and Oura both pursue preventive health collaborations with Abu Dhabi authorities. Ultrahuman and ADPHC will spend the next two years on research and clinical validation before a phased public rollout.

launches.title: Google announces the Fitbit Edge, a middle ground between Pixel Watch 5 and Fitbit Air
launches.excerpt: Google is releasing the Fitbit Edge, a new fitness tracker positioned between the Pixel Watch 5 and the Fitbit Air. Priced at $180, the device features a pill-shaped 1.34-inch OLED touch display housed in a slender aluminium frame with IP68 water and dust resistance. It is compatible with both Android and iPhones through the Google Health app and offers a battery life of roughly seven days when the always-on display is disabled. The tracker includes a single tactile side button and runs a fitness-focused operating system that supports phone notification mirroring, though it lacks a microphone, speaker, NFC, and downloadable apps or watch faces. For health and fitness tracking, the Edge is equipped with on-device GPS, an ECG, a blood oxygen sensor, an altimeter, an optical heart rate sensor, and a skin temperature sensor. Data is transmitted via Bluetooth 5.4 to the Google Health app, which integrates with the Gemini-powered Health Coach chatbot through a subscription service. The device is available for preorder in four colours ahead of its shipping date on October 27, with a Stephen Curry Special Edition also offered for $220. Users can pair multiple Google wearables with the Health app simultaneously without needing to manually switch devices. Additionally, the Edge is Google's first repairable fitness tracker, featuring a replaceable battery serviced through professional options rather than user disassembly.

launches.title: Prime Video unveils Blade Runner 2099 full trailer at NYCC
launches.excerpt: Prime Video revealed the full trailer for the upcoming sci-fi series Blade Runner 2099 at New York Comic-Con, following an initial teaser shown at San Diego Comic-Con. Co-stars Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer appeared alongside showrunner Silka Luisa during the panel to discuss the project. Set fifty years after the events of Blade Runner 2049, the narrative explores a world where a replicant uprising has occurred and humans have lost, prompting questions about the end of the human species. Yeoh portrays a dying replicant named Olwen, while Schafer stars as Cora, supported by a large ensemble cast in undisclosed roles. Prime Video is scheduled to release all eight episodes of the series on November 25, 2026. Additionally, a new trailer was debuted for Godzilla Minus Zero, the sequel to Takashi Yamazaki’s Godzilla Minus One. Set two years after the events of the previous film, the story follows a recovering Japan as a new threat emerges to shatter the hard-won peace. Most of the principal cast members from the original film are returning to reprise their roles for the sequel. Godzilla Minus Zero is set for a theatrical release on November 3, 2026. Meanwhile, Legendary Pictures has also scheduled the Monsterverse sequel Godzilla x Kong: Supernova for release in 2027.

launches.title: AWS Security Hub now exports findings to S3 in CSV or JSON format
launches.excerpt: AWS Security Hub has introduced support for exporting security findings directly to Amazon S3 in either CSV or JSON format. Security teams requiring findings outside the main console for compliance reporting and audit evidence can now utilise this feature without needing to build and maintain custom extraction pipelines. Users are able to initiate an export on demand directly from any findings page currently being viewed within the Security Hub console. This capability applies to various sections including Threats, Exposure, Vulnerabilities, Posture Management, Sensitive Data, and All Findings. Once initiated, Security Hub delivers the exported results straight to a designated S3 bucket located within the user's account. Organisations can select the CSV option when there is a requirement to review or share findings within a spreadsheet application. Alternatively, the JSON export option provides data formatted according to the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework. This new findings export functionality is now accessible across all AWS Regions where AWS Security Hub is currently available. Further information regarding this feature can be found by consulting the official AWS Security Hub User Guide.

launches.title: Amazon EC2 R8gd instances are now available in additional regions
launches.excerpt: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud R8gd instances are now available in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud Germany region. Powered by AWS Graviton4 processors, these instances deliver up to thirty percent better performance compared to previous Graviton3-based instances. They feature up to 11.4 terabytes of local NVMe-based solid-state drive block-level storage and are designed for applications requiring high-speed, low-latency local storage. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instances are offered in twelve different sizes to suit various workload requirements. They provide up to 50 gigabits per second of network bandwidth and up to 40 gigabits per second of bandwidth to Amazon Elastic Block Store. Customers can adjust their network and Amazon EBS bandwidth by 25 percent using EC2 instance bandwidth weighting configuration. This capability allows for greater flexibility when allocating bandwidth resources to optimise specific workloads. Furthermore, the instances offer Elastic Fabric Adapter networking support on the 24xlarge, 48xlarge, metal-24xl, and metal-48xl sizes. Users can manage these new deployments through the AWS Management Console and access migration resources via the AWS Graviton Fast Start program.

geo.title: US federal agents raid home of Democratic congresswoman and Trump critic Ilhan Omar
geo.excerpt: US federal agents searched the Washington home of Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar on Monday as part of a criminal investigation. Agents from Homeland Security Investigations conducted the search three weeks before midterm elections that will determine control of Congress. The operation was linked to a criminal fraud investigation concerning immigration paperwork submitted on behalf of the Somali-born lawmaker by her late father when she was a child. Border enforcement chief Tom Homan confirmed that a warrant was executed and that an investigation had been ongoing for a while. The Department of Justice confirmed that agents carried out a court-authorised search in the Washington area, though officials did not explicitly identify Omar or detail the exact nature of the probe. Several agents wearing HSI jackets were seen outside the congresswoman's residence as the search began around 6:00am. Omar, a leftist Democrat and vocal critic of Donald Trump, has previously dismissed allegations against her as politically motivated attacks. There was no immediate public response from Omar to the search, and her office and the administration were sought for comment by news agencies. No charges have been announced against Omar in connection with the enforcement action.

geo.title: Cyber-attack defrosts refrigerators in two French supermarket chains
geo.excerpt: French supermarket chains Intermarché and Cooperative U have been targeted by a large-scale cyber-attack that remotely caused their refrigerators to defrost. An estimated 150 to 200 Intermarché shops and nearly 100 Cooperative U outlets were affected by the incident. Reports from BFM TV indicate that France’s largest supermarket chain, E. Leclerc, was also impacted, though the company did not immediately confirm this information. Paris prosecutors confirmed that the attack had also prompted outbreaks of fire in some stores. Affected branches face significant financial losses and will have to discard all of their fresh and frozen products. Cooperative U chief executive Dominique Schelcher described the incident as unprecedented and extremely serious, noting that refrigeration systems had been disrupted since Sunday night. Company teams are currently working to restore normal operations as quickly as possible. The Paris prosecutor’s office has opened an official investigation to identify victims, establish the link between the cyber-attack and the reported damage, and examine the foodstuff losses and fires. Intermarché condemned the resulting food waste and warned that insurance policies may not cover this specific type of in-store incident. The cyber-attack occurs amid growing concern across Europe regarding malicious digital intrusions, prompting French President Emmanuel Macron to order heightened measures to protect critical national infrastructure from potential hybrid threats.

geo.title: Indian opposition figures lead march through Delhi as police again obstruct protests
geo.excerpt: Thousands of people marched through Delhi led by opposition figures and student groups to demand the resignation of India’s chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar. The demonstration followed weekend unrest that resulted in mass detentions by police during protests organised by the Gen Z Cockroach movement. Protesters aimed to submit a petition to the supreme court calling for Kumar to step down over a voter roll verification process that has seen more than 130 million names deleted since last year. Opposition parties and civil society groups allege that this special intensive revision disproportionately affects Muslim voters and minorities to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government and the Bharatiya Janata party. The election commission has denied favouring any party and stated that improperly deleted voters can re-enrol, while the BJP has accused opponents of undermining democracy. Police barricades and closures of central metro stations prevented thousands of protesters from getting within 600 metres of the supreme court on Monday. Nevertheless, lawyers successfully submitted the petition on behalf of opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, who later breached the barricades to reach the court gates by evening. Gandhi accused the government of electoral cheating and commended the ongoing youth-led uprising. Other opposition figures also condemned the voter deletions and vowed to continue demonstrations until Kumar resigns and the government is removed.

geo.title: Saudi minister vows 'serious response' to Houthi attacks on airports
geo.excerpt: Saudi Arabia's energy minister, Prince Abdul Aziz bin Salman, has promised a serious response to recent deadly attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement on the kingdom's airports and energy facilities. Speaking at the WPC Energy Congress in Riyadh, the prince acknowledged that energy security cannot be taken for granted and that recent events had tested the nation's infrastructure and resilience. The remarks followed a wave of Houthi missile and drone strikes, including an attack on Terminal 4 of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Sunday that killed a Pakistani resident. That incident came a day after another missile strike on Terminal 3 of the same airport killed 13 people, including multiple foreign nationals and Saudi citizens. Further attacks targeted King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, along with various oil and gas installations, though no casualties were reported in Dammam. The Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea stated that the operations were launched in retaliation for Saudi air strikes in Yemen and warned airlines against using Saudi airspace. The escalating violence has drawn widespread international condemnation, with United Nations Secretary General António Guterres warning that attacks on civilian infrastructure violate international law. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump stated he would make a decision regarding potential US involvement in strikes against the Houthis, and Iran called for dialogue to resolve the crisis. The ongoing conflict has intensified following the unravelling of an informal ceasefire in July, severely impacting regional stability and global oil prices.

geo.title: Nobel economics prize awarded to Robert Hall and Michael ⁠Woodford
geo.excerpt: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences has been awarded to American academics Robert Hall and Michael Woodford for their research on how monetary and fiscal policy can help stabilise economic fluctuations. Announced on Monday by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, the prize is the final award to be presented this year. The two laureates developed macroeconomic models that improve the implementation of stabilisation policies, which help reduce damaging economic swings. According to the Committee for the Prize in Economic Sciences, their work provides a stable theoretical foundation for models currently used by central banks and governments globally. These developments help authorities manage economic shocks such as energy crises and sudden shifts in household consumption. Hall and Woodford created new tools during the 1970s oil crises after existing Keynesian models ceased working effectively during recessions. Rather than relying solely on statistical links between variables like inflation and production, they built their models on microeconomic foundations that incorporate the actions of individual households and businesses. Established by Sweden's central bank in 1969, the economics prize includes a diploma, a gold medal, and a $1.2m cheque. The prize follows last week's announcements of the Nobel awards for medicine, physics, chemistry, literature, and peace.

invest.title: Time to tell US raider Saba Capital to get lost – again | Nils Pratley
invest.excerpt: New York hedge fund Saba Capital has built a stake approaching thirty percent in the FTSE 250 investment trust Baillie Gifford US Growth Trust, known as USA. Led by Boaz Weinstein, the hedge fund is attempting to install three non-independent nominees on the trust board during the upcoming annual meeting. Regular shareholders have already rejected Saba twice over the past eighteen months. The trust has delivered an annualised return of 16.7 percent since its launch in 2018, outperforming the S&P 500, though its five-year statistics were affected by artificial intelligence valuation shifts in late 2022. The trust portfolio includes prominent holdings such as Anthropic, Databricks, OpenAI, SpaceX and Stripe. Saba has proposed offering shareholders a one hundred percent cash exit near net asset value, but the trust board states it previously offered Saba an equivalent exit price, which the fund declined. Brokers Investec and Panmure Liberum warn that Saba lacks a credible plan and that not voting constitutes a vote for the hedge fund. An assumed sympathiser, Sessa Capital, holds an additional 7.7 percent stake. The annual meeting is scheduled for 23 October, with platform voting deadlines arriving even earlier.

invest.title: India’s retail inflation jumps to 5.54% in September, above estimates
invest.excerpt: India's headline retail inflation rose to 5.54% in September from 4.82% in August, exceeding economists' expectations of 5.40% according to a Reuters poll. This increase marked the eleventh consecutive month of rising inflation in the country, reaching a 22-month high and prompting pressure on the central bank to tighten monetary policy. Data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Program Implementation showed that food inflation climbed to 7.74% in September from 5.97% the previous month, with prices increasing more rapidly in rural areas than in urban locations. Transport costs also surged, as goods transport inflation rose by 14.73% and personal transport inflation jumped by 7.46%. The Reserve Bank of India recently raised interest rates for the first time since 2023, signalling that further rate cuts are off the table in the near term. India remains vulnerable to supply disruptions due to its heavy reliance on imported fuel, while ongoing Middle East tensions and concerns surrounding Hurricane Isaias keep oil prices elevated. Additionally, the agricultural sector faces severe risks from a Super El Nino weather pattern, which resulted in the country's lowest rainfall in over a decade during the crucial monsoon season. This drought has left several farming states, including Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Punjab, and Haryana, facing extreme dry conditions. The central bank anticipates headline inflation to average 5.2% for the financial year ending March 2027, remaining above its 4% medium-term target. Meanwhile, HSBC analysts have predicted that the Reserve Bank of India will implement another interest rate hike in December in response to the sustained inflationary pressures.

invest.title: Labour has got the message – developing nations suffer most from bond market turmoil | Heather Stewart
invest.excerpt: Recent bond market turmoil driven by conflicts in the Middle East and heavy borrowing by the United States has severely impacted developing countries, which are already struggling with energy crises and climate adaptation costs. Finance ministers and central bankers have been gathering in Bangkok for annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank to address these financial pressures. Even before recent market shifts, experts noted that debt servicing consumed 45 percent of government revenues in the global south and 70 percent in low-income nations. While the current G20 chair under Donald Trump has focused primarily on global economic growth, the UK presidency next year will prioritize unsustainable debt. Foreign secretary Ed Miliband has stated that the UK will use its G20 presidency to mobilise international efforts, echoing previous debt relief achievements under the last Labour government in 2005. However, government officials acknowledge that current circumstances are more complex because much of the debt is now held by private creditors rather than governments. A proposed plan by the thinktank Development Finance International suggests giving 27 heavily burdened countries a ten-year debt service holiday by cutting interest rates and extending loan terms. This initiative would cost approximately $13 billion a year, primarily affecting private creditors who would need to be coaxed or legislated into participation. The plan also proposes relief for small island developing states facing extreme weather events. British ministers have indicated they are open to such proposals and prepared to use the UK diplomatic weight to address the challenge.

invest.title: UK savings: 5% interest rate deals may not last, say experts
invest.excerpt: National Savings and Investments has raised returns on some of its British savings bonds, with many accounts now paying more than 5% for the first time in nearly three years. The provider offers fixed interest rates over one, two, three, and five-year terms for both new customers and those with maturing accounts. Growth bond rates now range from 4.99% for the one-year product up to 5.17% for the five-year option, while income bonds pay out monthly. Financial experts note that while these rates are competitive, higher yields can sometimes be found elsewhere with lesser-known banking institutions. A key advantage of NS&I bonds is that investors can deposit up to £1 million per person, with 100% of the savings secured by the Treasury. However, money invested in these fixed-term bonds cannot be withdrawn early, meaning savers may prefer to keep emergency funds in high-paying easy-access accounts. Other institutions have also adjusted their offerings recently, such as Starling bank launching a 5% rate on its Easy Saver account for eligible customers and Marcus by Goldman Sachs increasing its one-year fixed-rate bond to 4.75%. Industry analysts caution that attractive savings deals in the current market may not remain available for long once providers secure enough cash.
